claims.original_statement: The first differential is the connecting map of successive filtration quotients; if d raises filtration, it is induced directly by d. The statement additionally assumes countable direct sums.
claims.proved_statement: Both conclusions hold for every filtered complex in any abelian category; countable direct sums are unnecessary.
claims.hypotheses: A is abelian; F is decreasing and d preserves it. For the second assertion, d(F^p K^n) is contained in F^{p+1}K^{n+1} for all p,n.
claims.exact_maps: The short exact sequence gr^{p+1}K -> F^pK/F^{p+2}K -> gr^pK has connecting map [z] -> [d^n z], of bidegree (1,0), without any cochain translation.
claims.example: Finite-dimensional vector spaces give an abelian category without countable coproducts; the representative proof still applies.
claims.propagation: Bounded receiving applications checked; no source formula changes or unrelated removal of hypotheses. The editorial supplement carries the stronger statement and exact maps.

dependencies.receiving_outcome: Part (2) applies to the stated filtration in an arbitrary abelian category. This lemma supplies no countable-sum requirement; the full independent derived-functor comparison and sign conventions are not certified by this bounded dependency check.
The cited successive-quotient short exact sequence gives d1 by the proved connecting-map formula. The module category already admits countable sums; all tensor and K-flatness hypotheses are retained.
